title: The Arclight Project Roadmap
text:
Note



Arclight follows the principles of MVP development and separation of concerns. Models are developed, validated, optimized, and released separately from the Flutter module. The Flutter module is designed to adapt to additional functionality unlocked by adding additional ML modules via the .tflite package.

title: The Arclight Project Roadmap
text:
Phase 1: Model Development & Optimization (Google Colab)
Train, validate, and optimize machine learning models within cloud notebook environments before exporting for on-device execution, publishing source code under an open-source license.

Tasks:

Colab Model Development: Develop, train, and validate initial ML models (such as text-to-speech tools extracting key outbreak parameters like location, time, symptoms, and descriptions) inside Google Colab.
Optimization & Quantization: Apply post-training quantization and model compression techniques to minimize memory footprint and optimize execution speed for target end-user devices.
TFLite Export: Export tuned models into the lightweight .tflite format required for mobile and desktop execution.
Open-Source Licensing: Host model source code and assets on GitHub under the GNU General Public License v3.0 (GPL v3.0).

title: The Arclight Project Roadmap
section: Phase 2: UI/UX Proof of Concept (Streamlit & Docker)
text:
Phase 2: UI/UX Proof of Concept (Streamlit & Docker)
Prototype the user interface and validate operational workflows quickly through a web-based Proof of Concept (POC).

Tasks:

Streamlit Prototype: Build a functional Streamlit interface to mock up layouts, data ingestion workflows, and visualization formats (maps, tables, epidemic curves).
Workflow Validation: Test end-to-end data processing, user interaction flows, and structured decision-support outputs within the Streamlit workspace.
Docker Containerization: Package the Streamlit application into a Docker container for isolated testing, streamlined sharing, and collecting feedback from epidemiologists and stakeholders.

title: The Arclight Project Roadmap
text:
Phase 3: Flutter Application Development & Integration
Construct the production cross-platform native application framework and integrate local machine learning models into the Dart pipeline.

Tasks:

App Scaffolding & Front-End: Develop responsive front-end UI components in Flutter supporting Android, iOS, and Windows targeting cross-platform consistency.
Dart Data Pipeline: Implement data import, sanitization, and preprocessing functions in Dart to prepare user inputs for model consumption.
On-Device Model Integration: Integrate exported .tflite models into the Flutter application via the tflite package in Dart for privacy-preserving, local execution.
Secure Local Storage: Implement encrypted local databases (e.g., SQLite or Hive) with local encrypted backups to external storage media like USB drives.

title: The Arclight Project Roadmap
text:
Phase 4: Integration Testing & Multi-Platform Deployment
Conduct rigorous system-wide testing and publish production application builds across supported platforms and repositories.

Tasks:

Integration Testing: Perform comprehensive integration testing across Android, iOS, and Windows, verifying on-device model accuracy, UI responsiveness, PHI censoring algorithms during PDF/CSV exports, and database security.
App Store & Open-Source Distribution: Publish finalized production binaries to app stores (Google Play Store, Apple App Store, Microsoft Store) and release full source code and build distributions on GitHub.

title: Welcome to the Arclight Project
text:
Arclight is an open-source, cross-platform, on-device machine learning and AI toolkit designed for use by epidemiologists, clinicians, and public health personnel investigating infectious disease outbreaks in novel populations and locations.
Whether the health emergency is a new outbreak of a bacterial infection, a novel virus, a drug-resistant fungus, an environmental toxin, or a bioterror attack, the first contact between pathogen and the public health system will be the outbreak investigation conducted by local health departments. The Arclight application provides front line public health professionals with actionable decision support tools, backstopped by robust machine learning and AI models.

title: What Is Arclight?
text:
NoteThe Problem



Practical implementation of machine learning and artificial intelligence is significantly lacking on the front lines of public health. While many proposed solutions show promise in controlled academic settings, actual implementation is challenged by data fragmentation, data bias, privacy concerns, domain oversights, or a reliance on computing infrastructure unavailable to under-resourced local health departments.
Whether the health emergency is a new outbreak of an existing pathogen, a novel virus, a drug-resistant fungus, an environmental toxin, or a bioterror attack, the first contact between pathogen and the public health system will be the outbreak investigation conducted by local health departments. The impact generated by aiding this process with ML/AI tools is considerable, and currently unaddressed.

title: What Is Arclight?
text:
Our Solution
Arclight is an open-source, cross-platform, on-device machine learning and AI toolkit for epidemiologists and public health professionals designed to provide decision support during an outbreak investigation.
In its final form, the application, running on an end-user’s device, will bring in information in the form of images, text, or audio, process the information locally, and generate outputs in the form of text, charts, graphs, maps, or other helpful decision support aides through the use of various machine learning and AI models.

title: What Is Arclight?
text:
Design Goals and Exclusions
Arclight will assist field epidemiologists and public health professionals when investigating potential infectious disease outbreaks. Arclight will exclusively process information on-device to protect PHI, eliminate infrastructure costs, and add direct oversight by the end-user.
Specific Arclight functions will evolve over time, but will generally will be designed to support epidemiologists during the following phases of an outbreak investigation:

Integrating existing public health surveillance data
Processing case reports and investigative notes
Refining the case definition based on collected information and alternative diagnoses
Organizing case reports based on population, location, and time
Developing etiological hypotheses based on observed notes and reference data.

Arclight deployment will include only Android, iOS, and Windows devices. Model performance will be constrained by the demands of on-device processing, to include available modules in the required tech stack. Arclight will not replace established decision support tools used for policy development, outbreak forecasting, or other use cases requiring large data sets and server-grade processing power; rather, it fills a gap at the local level.

title: What Is Arclight?
text:
Technical Methodology and Implementation
Arclight’s architecture is built on a modular, cross-platform framework that prioritizes on-device execution to ensure absolute privacy for Protected Health Information (PHI) and independence from cloud infrastructure. The methodology for integrating machine learning capabilities into the application is divided into model development and front-end integration.

Model Development and Export
Each machine learning and AI model is developed independently as a standalone module to ensure ease of testing, rapid iteration, and separation of concerns.

Environment: Models are developed using Google Colab.
Framework: TensorFlow is utilized for model training, evaluation, and optimization.
Optimization & Export: Once trained, models are optimized for mobile and desktop on-device execution and exported into the lightweight TensorFlow Lite (.tflite) format. Trained models are available for integration into other applications under GNU Public License v3.0.



Flutter and Dart Integration
The core application is built using the Flutter framework, enabling a single codebase to deploy across Android, iOS, and Windows. For each machine learning function or utility module, a standardized, sequential process is followed within the Dart codebase:

Front-End Design: Develop the responsive front-end user interface components in Flutter to capture inputs (text, audio, images).
Data Import & Preprocessing: Write robust data ingestion and preprocessing handlers in Dart to prepare inputs for model compatibility.
Model Execution: Invoke the exported .tflite model locally using the tflite package for Dart, passing the preprocessed inputs to the model.
Output Formatting: Capture the inference results, process and format them (generating charts, tables, maps, or textual decision support), and display them within the UI.

This modular workflow is replicated dynamically for every machine learning model integrated into Arclight.
